methods.label: Factor and cancel
methods.explanation:
The terms containing \(a\) and \(b\) in the numerator form a perfect square. Grouping them reveals a difference of squares:
\[
\begin{aligned}
a^2+b^2-c^2+2ab
&=(a+b)^2-c^2\\
&=(a+b-c)(a+b+c).
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominator has the same useful structure:
\[
\begin{aligned}
a^2+c^2-b^2+2ac
&=(a+c)^2-b^2\\
&=(a-b+c)(a+b+c).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the original denominator is nonzero precisely when
\[
a+b+c\ne0
\quad\text{and}\quad
a-b+c\ne0.
\]
Under these restrictions, we may divide numerator and denominator by the common nonzero factor \(a+b+c\), obtaining
\[
\frac{(a+b-c)(a+b+c)}{(a-b+c)(a+b+c)}
=\boxed{\frac{a+b-c}{a-b+c}}.
\]
Both restrictions must be retained after cancellation. The answer is choice E.
